name: Seeti Counter
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer 3V (stock 140)
works_why: Mic front end and clap/whistle detector are analog and tuned on synthetic audio; the firmware itself passes 115 host checks; the documented limit is that quiet whistles are missed.
first: Bench-test the microphone gain with real claps before ordering more than 5 boards.

name: Gas Taraju (LPG cylinder scale)
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer (stock 140)
works_why: HX711 load-cell chain is a standard circuit; accuracy depends on the cell, mounting and calibration, which only a build can show.
first: Calibrate with a known weight; check drift over a day.

name: Fridge Door Guard
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer (stock 140); D4 TVS 5V bidir (stock 175)
works_why: Reed switch, timer and buzzer: simple circuit, simple firmware; TVS and input conditioning follow standard practice.
first: Test the reed gap and the 2-minute alarm on the bench.

name: Bijli Meter Reader
order_why: all parts live-checked, none flagged
works_why: Optical pulse reading of a meter LED depends on the sensor alignment and ambient light; circuit is standard.
first: Try on a real meter with a shroud before enclosure work.

name: Bijli Log
order_why: all parts live-checked, none flagged
works_why: Current/voltage logging front end is analog and uncalibrated; mains-adjacent measurement needs isolation care.
first: Do not connect to mains until a qualified electrician reviews the isolation; start with a bench supply.

name: Chulha Timers
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer (stock 140)
works_why: Multi-timer with buttons, LEDs and buzzer; simple circuit; firmware tested on the host.
first: Check button debounce and the buzzer volume on the first board.

name: Rain Alert Bell + plate
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer 85dB (stock 140); D3 TVS 5V bidir (stock 175); D4 TVS 5V bidir (stock 175)
works_why: Conductive rain plate corrodes and drifts; electronics are simple and protected with TVS.
first: Use the plate for a week outdoors before deciding on a coating.

name: Tap Litre Meter
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer (stock 140); D4 TVS 5V bidir (stock 175)
works_why: Hall/flow-pulse counting is standard; the litres-per-pulse constant depends on the flow sensor.
first: Calibrate against a measured bucket.

works_why: Laser-cut stand: fit depends on kerf; stability limit stated.

order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing
works_why: Printed game; needs language and fact review before print.

name: 2 Kalakriti Automata (laser)
order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing
works_why: Laser cut files regenerated with correct kerf compensation (outlines outward, holes inward, gear backlash only once); cam and gear checks PASS; frame layouts and figure artwork are still first-pass.

name: 3 Prayog STEM lab kit
order_why: all parts live-checked, none flagged
works_why: Educational kit with a straightforward MCU board; 40 host checks on the statistics and command code.

name: 4 Jal-Rakshak tank controller
order_why: limited stock on: J1 12 V DC in (stock 321)
works_why: Low-voltage board reuses the Kheti-Mitra 12 V front end and pump driver; the firmware rules pass 20 simulated checks and an 8 MHz PCB build exists (3.2 kB); real probes, water, pump currents untested; the mains version is still out of scope.
first: Bench test with a 12 V pump and probes in a bucket; never connect mains.

name: 5 Kheti-Mitra irrigation
order_why: limited stock on: J1 12 V DC in (stock 321)
works_why: Irrigation controller with 12 V switching and soil sensing; 22 host checks pass; field conditions (water, sun, surge) are the risk.
first: Run with a lamp as the load for 48 hours before any valve or pump.

name: 6 Gas-Suraksha leak alarm
order_why: all parts live-checked, none flagged
works_why: Prototype/logging board carries the tested alarm engine (34 checks) with an active buzzer and a UART log header; MQ-6 thresholds are placeholders and it is not a certified detector.

name: 01 Reflex Raja

name: 03 Aloo Bomb

name: 05 Rangoli Spiro Gears
order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing

order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing
works_why: Cut file now kerf-compensated (wheels, axle holes, band slots at nominal size); simple mechanism.

name: 09 Marble Cricket
order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing
works_why: Cut file now kerf-compensated (peg holes at 6.2 mm press fit); pocket scoring needs a calibration drop.
first: Cut one, drop 200 marbles and check the pocket distribution.

name: 10 Katha Cubes
order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing
works_why: Cube net and the 36 words ready; Hindi and Telugu checked for consistency (grandmother term aligned, gender-neutral problem phrases) but a native-speaker review is still required before print; icons are optional for the prototype.
first: Print text-only cubes for the prototype; get the words reviewed by native speakers before the production print.

name: KINETIC motion controller + vibration puck
order_why: all parts live-checked, none flagged
works_why: ESP32-S3 controller with three StepStick sockets and a 24 V to 5 V buck. Motion library (370 checks) and protocol are host-tested; the ESP32 firmware now compiles for the ESP32-S3 with 0 warnings but has not run on hardware; drivers and motors are bought in. The vibration model is trained on synthetic data only.
first: Power with a current-limited supply and no drivers; then one driver and one motor at low current.

name: MITTI-NETRA soil + structure node
order_why: all parts live-checked, none flagged
works_why: Charger thermal pad now grounded with thermal vias; NTC window stops Li-ion charging outside about 6 to 44 C; power diodes corrected; IP65 box with a printed mounting plate; firmware core 23 checks and the pin map match; the cellular modem is a plug-in breakout and the ESP32 firmware compiles for the ESP32-S3 with 0 warnings (not yet run on hardware).
first: Bring up power and charging first (check TEMP voltage at room temperature), then the modem last.

name: BioTray vertical-farm controller
order_why: limited stock on: J2 12 V DC in (stock 321)
works_why: 12 V low-side drivers, ESP32 and sensors; 22 host checks; calibration constants are placeholders; wet environment.
first: Dummy loads on all outputs first; seal the enclosure before any water.

name: BioWatt MFC harvester
order_why: all parts verified; the BQ25570 stock is limited (about 400) and the hold capacitor is a substitute grade
works_why: BQ25570 with megohm setting dividers computed from datasheet equations; cold start needs at least 600 mV (marginal for one microbial fuel cell); the hold capacitor is X7R where the datasheet asks for low leakage; leakage on a dirty board shifts the thresholds.
first: Test with a bench supply at 0.8 V first, clean flux thoroughly, then try the fuel cell.

name: GEONODE foundation monitoring
order_why: uses other boards plus bought-in modules; each module's pinout must be checked against its datasheet
works_why: Detector logic and feature code are host-tested (54 checks) but on synthetic vibration; the crack signature is an assumption; node hardware is the MITTI-NETRA board with a LoRa module.
first: Record real vibration for a week and re-derive the thresholds before trusting any alarm.

name: AQUAPONICS controller
order_why: uses other boards plus bought-in modules; each module's pinout must be checked against its datasheet
works_why: Control and forecasting core passes 13 checks; biological limits are placeholders; no ammonia or nitrite sensing; live animals depend on it.
first: Run a week with water only; tune limits with an aquaculture expert before any fish.

name: SORTER bio-robotic platform
order_why: uses other boards plus bought-in modules; each module's pinout must be checked against its datasheet
works_why: Tracking core passes 28 checks; the vision is a colour-rule baseline tested on synthetic discs; the gripper geometry is untested; machine guarding is your responsibility.
first: Image real produce under fixed light and replace the classifier before building the conveyor.

name: AGROVER solar rover
order_why: uses other boards plus bought-in modules; each module's pinout must be checked against its datasheet
works_why: Navigation and power core pass 19 simulated-field checks; dead-reckoning only; chassis plates untested with real motors; needs a safety review and an emergency stop.
first: Drive on blocks first, then slowly in a clear area with the stop in hand.

name: Jal-Netra (engineering marvel)
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer (stock 140)
works_why: Clamp-on ultrasonic transit-time measurement has a hard analog front end; the manual itself says Gate 1 acoustic test comes first and it is not sellable.
first: Run the Gate 1 acoustic test with the evaluation setup before any more boards.

name: ASTRADAND gesture wand (sci-fi project)
order_why: substitute addressable LED whose pad geometry is unproven; other parts verified
works_why: IMU gesture recognition validated against a Python reference (46/46) and on synthetic gestures; hardware (haptics, six addressable LEDs) is new; the LED part was replaced with a pin-compatible one whose pads are unproven.
first: Order 2 boards, check the LED footprint fit, then run the gesture self-test.

name: Gravity toys (5)
order_why: no electronic parts to source: local laser-cutting or printing
works_why: All five toys now have prototype drawings (Santulan lathe drawing, marble-tower posts and groove spec, ramp-racer car and ladder stand, Galton assembly guide, Drop Quest v1 rules with 60 solver-verified levels and laser parts); physics checks PASS; none built or play-tested.
first: Cut or turn one of each and play-test; measure ramp times and marble behaviour.

name: Wave 1 electronics toys
order_why: limited stock on: BZ1 Buzzer (stock 140)
works_why: AP1 board added (ATmega328P, MP3 module socket, bought-in 4-digit 74HC595 display module on a 5-way lead, 7-LED ball lane on a 74HC595, 7-button resistor ladder, lamp and motor drivers); all three apps now build for the board (about 6 kB each) and pass 76 host checks. The MP3 command codes are from memory and must be checked on the real module; the ladder thresholds are calculated, not measured.
first: Bench-test one board per product: ladder readings, MP3 commands, display module polarity (one compile flag each).

name: Prototype packs (10)
